title_en: Laoshan Sub-bureau of Land and Resources, Qingdao Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Management v. Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over a land use right grant contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. For a contract where the expression of intent of both parties is genuine, the agreed content does not harm the lawful rights and interests of the state, the collective, or any third party, and the contract has been notarized, it shall be deemed to have been established.

full_text_en:
Qingdao Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration

Laoshan Sub-bureau of Land Resources v. Qingdao Qiankun

Wood Industry Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Land Use Right Grant Contract

[2024] SPC Civil Final Judgment No. 84

【Ruling Summary】

I. A contract that reflects the true intent of both parties, whose agreed terms do not harm the legitimate rights and interests of the state, the collective, or third parties, and which has been notarized, shall be deemed to have been validly formed.

II. According to the relevant provisions of the Contract Law, a contract lawfully formed shall become effective upon its formation. Where laws or administrative regulations require approval, registration, or other formalities for the contract to become effective, such provisions shall be followed.

III. If part of a contract is invalid but does not affect the validity of the remaining parts, the remaining parts of the contract shall be deemed valid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 84

Appellant (Original Defendant): Qingdao Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration, Laoshan Sub-bureau of Land Resources (formerly Qingdao Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources), domiciled at: 3rd Floor, Office Building, Shilaoren Community Residents Committee, Laoshan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Hao, Director of the Bureau.

Authorized Agent: Meng Fansheng, Lawyer of Beijing Zhongjing Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Zhao Shanke, Staff Member of the Bureau.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Gouya Village, Beizhai Sub-district Office, Laoshan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Guofeng, Chairman of the Company.

Authorized Agent: Ma Xu, Lawyer of Beijing Dacheng Law Firm, Jinan Branch.

The appellant, Qingdao Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration, Laoshan Sub-bureau of Land Resources (hereinafter referred to as the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2006) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 8 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court in a dispute over a land use right grant contract with the respondent, Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qiankun Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on October 24, 2007. The authorized agents of the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau, Meng Fansheng and Zhao Shanke, and the legal representative of Qiankun Company, Jiang Guofeng, and its authorized agent, Ma Xu, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

The facts found at first instance: On May 29, 2000, the People's Government of Laoshan District, Qingdao City, submitted a "Request for the First Batch of Urban Construction Land in 2000" to the Qingdao Municipal People's Government. The request stated: In accordance with the "Overall Land Use Plan of Laoshan District," the district planned to convert 126,666 square meters of orchard land in Gouya Village and 6,667 square meters of orchard land in Hongyuan Village, totaling 133,333 square meters, for the first batch of land. The above-mentioned land had been designated as urban construction land in the "Overall Land Use Plan of Laoshan District." After completing the procedures for converting agricultural land to construction land and requisitioning it as state-owned, the district would further approve the land according to the land approval authority and specific construction projects. Subsequently, the Qingdao Municipal People's Government submitted the "Request for the First Batch of Urban Construction Land in Laoshan District in 2000" (Qingzheng Di Fa [2000] No. 267) to the Shandong Provincial People's Government.

On February 28, 2001, Qiankun Company and the Beizhai Sub-district Office entered into a "Land Use Right Grant Agreement." The agreement provided that the Beizhai Sub-district Office would grant Qiankun Company the right to use approximately 150 mu of land in the Beizhai Industrial Park (west of Songling Road, north of Maigou Road), with a term of 50 years, at a land price of 68,800 yuan per mu, totaling approximately 10.32 million yuan. After the contract was signed, based on relevant documents of the Laoshan District People's Government in 1999, Qiankun Company paid land grant deposits of 1.8 million yuan and 500,000 yuan on April 20, 2001, and September 5, 2001, respectively, to the Land Planning and Mineral Resources Management Office of the Beizhai Sub-district Office (hereinafter referred to as the Land Management Office), an agency of the former Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources. The Land Management Office issued receipts. On August 25, 2001, Qiankun Company delivered a check of 2.58 million yuan to the Land Management Office, which issued a receipt for 2.58 million yuan. The funds were actually transferred to the Land Management Office on March 27, 2003.

On September 10, 2001, Qiankun Company obtained the "Notice of Environmental Review for Fixed Construction Projects" ([2001] Qinglao Huan Yu Ding Zi No. 10) issued by the Qingdao Laoshan District Environmental Protection Bureau. On September 28, 2001, it obtained the "Notice of Fixed-Point Construction Projects in Villages and Towns of Laoshan District, Qingdao" (Qinglao Cun Gui Ding Zi [2001] No. 045) issued by the Qingdao Laoshan District Village and Town Planning and Construction Administration Office. On September 29, 2001, it obtained the "Construction Land Planning Permit" (Laoshan Jian Cun Zi No. 045) issued by the same office, confirming that the land use project complied with urban planning requirements and permitting the handling of procedures for requisitioned and allocated land. On the same day, it also obtained the "Notice of Planning and Design Requirements for Village and Town Planning Construction Projects in Laoshan District, Qingdao" (Qinglao Cun Gui She Zi [2001] No. 045) from the same office. On September 30, 2001, the Qingdao Laoshan District Development and Planning Bureau, based on the project application from the Economic and Trade Office of the Beizhai Sub-district Office, issued a "Reply on Approving the Project for the New Plant Construction of Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd." (Laoshan Ji Xiang Zi [2001] No. 96). On the same day, the Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources issued a "Statement on Land Use by Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd.," which stated: "Regarding the 150 mu of industrial land of Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd. in the Beizhai Industrial Park, due to the adjustment of the Beizhai Industrial Park plan, upon application by the Beizhai Sub-district Office, our bureau agreed to adjust the company's land to 215 mu. The land procedures for the company are currently being processed."

On January 31, 2002, the Shandong Provincial People's Government issued the "Reply of the Shandong Provincial People's Government on the Urban Construction Land of Laoshan District, Qingdao" (Lu Zheng Tu Zi [2002] No. 35), which stated: "The Laoshan District Land Administration Bureau of Qingdao plans to requisition 133,333 square meters (equivalent to 200 mu) of orchard land in two villages, including Gouya Village, Beizhai Sub-district, as reserved land for urban construction by the Laoshan District Government of Qingdao. Upon review, the land in this batch complies with the overall land use plan of Laoshan District, Qingdao, and has been included in the annual land use plan of your city. The submitted plan for converting agricultural land and the requisition plan are feasible, and this batch of land is approved."

On January 16, 2003, the former Qingdao Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources and Qiankun Company entered into the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" (Qinglao Tu He Zi [2003] No. 4). The contract stipulated that the land granted by the Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources to Qiankun Company was located north of Maigou Road and west of Songling Road, Gouya Village, Beizhai Sub-district, with a total land area of 175,907 square meters, of which the granted land area was 146,383 square meters. The purpose of the granted land under this contract was industrial use. The term of the land use right under this contract was 50 years. The land grant fee under this contract was 103.20 yuan per square meter, totaling 18,153,602.40 yuan. Within 60 days from the signing of this contract, the grantee shall pay the entire land grant fee in a lump sum... The contract also provided that within 30 days from the date of full payment of the land grant fee as agreed in the contract, the grantee shall, holding this contract and the payment voucher for the land grant fee, apply to the grantor for land registration in accordance with regulations and obtain the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" to acquire the granted land use right. The grantor shall, within 30 days from the date of the grantee's application for land registration, handle the registration of the granted land use right for the grantee in accordance with the law and issue the "State-owned Land Use Certificate." The grantee must pay the land grant fee on time according to the contract. If the grantee fails to pay the land grant fee on time, from the date of default, the grantee shall pay a late payment penalty of 3‰ of the overdue amount per day to the grantor. If the delay in payment exceeds six months, the grantor has the right to terminate the contract and recover the land, and the grantee has no right to demand the return of the deposit, and the grantor may also request the grantee to compensate for other losses caused by the breach. The grant plan for the land under this contract is subject to approval by the Shandong Provincial People's Government, and this contract shall become effective on the date of such approval. Matters not covered in this contract may be agreed upon by both parties as annexes to the contract, which shall have the same legal effect as this contract. On the same day, the parties signed a "Supplementary Agreement" regarding the area and cost of the roads and green belts to be requisitioned on behalf of the government. On February 18, 2003, both parties jointly applied for notarization of the above contract and agreement at the Qingdao Notary Public Office. On March 26, 2003, Qiankun Company delivered a check of 3 million yuan to the Land Management Office, which issued a receipt for 3 million yuan, but the funds were not actually transferred. The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau now confirmed that it had actually received a total of 4.88 million yuan in land grant fees from Qiankun Company. Thereafter, Qiankun Company did not pay the remaining land grant fee. Part of the 146,383 square meters of granted land under the above contract had been approved for conversion to construction land by Lu Zheng Tu Zi [2002] No. 35.

On June 6, 2005, the former Qingdao Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources, on the grounds that Qiankun Company failed to pay the full land grant fee on time as agreed in the contract and that the project land violated Qingdao Municipal Government Document [2003] No. 95, issued the "Decision of the Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources on Revoking the State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" (Laoshan Tu [2005] No. 139), deciding to revoke the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" signed with Qiankun Company on January 16, 2003, and requiring Qiankun Company to hold the original contract and go to the bureau within 10 days from receipt of the decision to handle matters related to rescission of the contract. The refund of paid amounts was to be handled at the Beizhai Sub-district Construction Service Center (formerly the Land Management Office of the Beizhai Sub-district Office). On June 7, 2005, the former Qingdao Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources delivered the above decision to Qiankun Company by express mail.

On March 13, 2006, the Qingdao Laoshan District Bureau of Land Resources was renamed the Qingdao Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration, Laoshan Sub-bureau of Land Resources.

During the first instance proceedings, the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau submitted a "Topographic Map of the Current Situation" of the land in question to the court, showing that the black line areas on the map were the topographic map after the signing of the land use right grant contract, and the red line-enclosed areas were the parts approved for conversion from agricultural to construction land. After cross-examination, Qiankun Company had no objection to this evidence.

Due to the unilateral rescission of the contract by the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau, Qiankun Company, after paying part of the grant fee, was unable to obtain the land under the contract. Qiankun Company believed that the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau had breached the contract, causing various economic losses of over 12 million yuan. Therefore, it filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting that the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau perform the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" (Qinglao Tu He Zi [2003] No. 4) and deliver all the land under the contract to Qiankun Company.

The court of first instance held that the land involved in the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" signed by both parties included a portion for which the approval procedure for converting agricultural land to construction land had been completed. According to Articles 43 and 44 of the "Land Administration Law," the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau had the right to grant that portion of land. The remaining portion had not been approved by the people's government and remained collectively-owned rural land, over which the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau had no right to dispose. Therefore, the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" signed by both parties was partially valid. Regarding the land grant fee paid by Qiankun Company: Before the contract was signed, Qiankun Company had paid a total of 4.88 million yuan in land grant fees to the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau. On March 26, 2003, Qiankun Company delivered a bank check of 3 million yuan to the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau, which issued a receipt. These actions indicated that Qiankun Company had been performing its contractual obligations. The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau's argument that the check was a bad check and could not be transferred was unsupported by evidence, and the court of first instance did not accept it. Regarding whether the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" should continue to be performed: Since part of the land under the contract had been approved by the Shandong Provincial People's Government, that portion was available for performance. Given that Qiankun Company's related project had been approved by relevant government authorities and had obtained project approval, planning, environmental protection, and other permits, the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau should deliver that portion of the land to it. The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau's defense that the contract should be rescinded had no legal basis, and the court of first instance did not support it.

In summary, the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" signed by both parties was partially valid. Qiankun Company had partially performed its payment obligations. The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau should deliver the land in question to Qiankun Company within the scope of the agricultural land converted to construction land approved by the government. Qiankun Company's claim that the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau should perform the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" (Qinglao Tu He Zi [2003] No. 4) and deliver all the land under the contract was partially established. In accordance with Articles 8, 56, and 107 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. The defendant, Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau, shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, deliver to the plaintiff, Qiankun Company, the land under the contract that has been approved for conversion to construction land (specific location subject to the "Reply of the Shandong Provincial People's Government on the Urban Construction Land of Laoshan District, Qingdao" (Lu Zheng Tu Zi [2002] No. 35) and the red line coordinates on the topographic map of the current situation); 2. The other claims of the plaintiff, Qiankun Company, are dismissed. Court costs of 160,778 yuan shall be borne by Qiankun Company in the amount of 130,070 yuan and by the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau in the amount of 30,708 yuan.

The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau believed that the first instance judgment erred in fact-finding and misapplied the law, so it appealed to this Court, requesting that the second instance set aside the first instance judgment, reject Qiankun Company's claims in accordance with the law, and order Qiankun Company to bear the litigation costs of both instances. The reasons were:

1. The first instance judgment's finding that the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" signed by both parties was partially valid was erroneous. (1) The subject matter of the contract—the land parcel—was indivisible property and did not allow for partial validity and partial invalidity. (2) The appellant did not have the right to dispose of the land, and the grant of the land in this case required approval from the Qingdao Municipal People's Government. (3) The grant plan for the land under this contract was subject to approval by the Shandong Provincial People's Government, and the contract would become effective on the date of such approval. Since the land in question had not yet completed the procedures for converting agricultural land to construction use, the conditions for drafting a grant plan and submitting it to the people's government for approval were not met. Therefore, the grant contract in this case had no legal effect, and the respondent only had an expectant right. (4) The first instance judgment ordering the appellant to grant partial land to the respondent violated the planning of the Qingdao Municipal People's Government. On November 11, 2003, the Qingdao Municipal People's Government approved a plan for the area including the land in question. According to that plan, the high-tech industrial zone should "appropriately extend northeastward to Lisha Road, and further extension into the Laoshan Scenic Area is strictly prohibited." The land under the grant contract was located in an area where construction was prohibited according to the Qingdao Municipal Government's plan. The approval documents for the 84 mu of land that had undergone the agricultural-to-construction conversion procedure had automatically become invalid.

2. The first instance judgment's finding that "the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau's defense that the contract should be rescinded had no legal basis" was erroneous. The appellant disputed the amount of the land grant fee paid by the respondent. Even if calculated at the 7.88 million yuan determined by the first instance, it accounted for only 43% of the total land grant fee of 18,153,602.4 yuan. The respondent failed to pay the full grant fee within six months after signing the contract. Pursuant to Articles 9 and 31 of the contract in question, the appellant had the right to terminate the contract, and Qiankun Company had received the decision to terminate. In accordance with Article 96 of the "Contract Law," the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract" was terminated when Qiankun Company received that decision. Since the contract did not specify a time limit for the appellant to exercise the right of termination, the appellant could exercise that right at any time after the conditions for termination were met.

3. The first instance judgment's determination of the amount of the land grant fee paid by the respondent was erroneous. The first instance judgment's finding that Qiankun Company paid 4.88 million yuan in land grant fees was erroneous and did not reflect the actual situation. After deducting the 3,813,357 yuan in land grant fees recovered by the Laoshan District People's Court, the amount of land grant fees paid by Qiankun Company should be determined as 1,066,643 yuan.

Qiankun Company argued in defense: 1. The first instance judgment's finding that the contract in question was partially valid had factual and legal basis, and the outcome was correct. The contract in question stipulated that the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau would deliver 215 mu of land to Qiankun Company, but only 84 mu were actually available for grant, which constituted a situation of partial invalidity. The transfer of approval authority referred to by the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau occurred after the contract was signed and did not affect the contract's validity. As for the new government plan emphasized by the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau, it only prohibited further extension into the scenic area, which did not affect the earlier contract. 2. The first instance judgment's finding that the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau's defense of contract rescission was unfounded was correct. The reason Qiankun Company did not pay the full amount was attributable to the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau. At the time, Qiankun Company's bank account had more than 7 million yuan in deposits, but the Land Management Office stopped accepting land grant fees, rendering Qiankun Company unable to perform. The conditions for the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau to unilaterally terminate the contract had not been met. The recovery of land grant fees by the Laoshan District People's Court occurred before the contract was rescinded and was irrelevant to this case. The Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau should continue to perform the contract.

Additional facts found at second instance: The bank check delivered by Qiankun Company to the Land Management Office on March 26, 2003, did not record the date of issue or the payee. Both parties had no dispute over this fact. This Court opined that, pursuant to Article 85 of the "Negotiable Instruments Law," the date of issue is a necessary item in a check, involving the calculation of the validity period of the check. A check without the date of issue should be deemed an invalid check.

The other facts found at second instance were the same as those found at first instance.

This Court opined that this case involved three issues: (1) the determination of the validity of the "State-owned Land Use Right Grant Contract"; (2) whether the first instance judgment correctly determined the amount of land grant fees paid by Qiankun Company; and (3) whether the Laoshan Land Resources Sub-bureau had the right to terminate the contract.

(1) Regarding the determination of the validity of the State-owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract. Although this contract stipulated that it would take effect only upon approval by the People's Government of Shandong Province, the 84 mu of land under the contract had already been approved by the People's Government of Shandong Province for conversion from agricultural land to construction land prior to the signing of the contract. Therefore, the lack of such approval for this portion does not affect the validity of the corresponding part of the contract. The remaining portion of the land under the contract had not yet undergone the approval procedures for conversion of agricultural land, and according to the contract, it had not yet taken effect and could not be transferred legally. The Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources argued that the contract had been formed but had not taken effect, and that it should not be deemed partially valid and partially invalid. This Court holds that the contract in question reflects the true intentions of both parties, its contents do not harm the lawful rights and interests of the State, the collective, or any third party, and it has been notarized. Therefore, it should be deemed to have been formed. Article 44 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A lawfully formed contract shall take effect upon its formation. Where laws or administrative regulations require approval, registration, or other formalities to be completed before a contract takes effect, such provisions shall govern." Article 44 of the Land Administration Law provides: "Where construction occupies land involving the conversion of agricultural land to construction land, approval procedures for the conversion of agricultural land shall be handled." Accordingly, the part of the contract concerning the land for which the government approval for conversion from agricultural land had not been obtained is held to be invalid. Pursuant to Article 56 of the Contract Law, if the invalidity of part of a contract does not affect the validity of the other parts, the other parts shall remain valid. Under the circumstances of this case, finding part of the contract invalid does not affect the validity of the other parts. Therefore, it should be held that the transfer of the use rights for the 84 mu of land that received government approval is valid, the transfer of the use rights for the 131 mu of land that did not receive government approval is invalid, and the other contract terms remain valid. This Court does not support the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources' appeal argument that the land transferred under the contract in question is indivisible and therefore the principle of partial validity and partial invalidity based on quantity is not applicable.

(2) Regarding the correctness of the amount of land transfer fees paid by Qiankun Company as determined by the court of first instance. The court of first instance found that Qiankun Company had paid land transfer fees of RMB 7.88 million to the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources, and Qiankun Company did not object to this finding. However, the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources only acknowledged receiving RMB 4.88 million in land transfer fees from Qiankun Company, and that RMB 3,813,357 had been deducted by the Laoshan District People's Court, leaving only RMB 1,066,643. The main dispute between the parties concerns whether a check for RMB 3 million delivered by Qiankun Company to the Land Management Office on March 26, 2003, should be counted as paid land transfer fees. Given that this check was deemed invalid due to the lack of a date of issue, and an invalid check cannot be used to transfer funds from Qiankun Company's bank account, Qiankun Company's act of issuing the check should be deemed an invalid civil act. Although the Land Management Office issued a receipt after receiving this check, because the check was invalid, the receipt issued by the Land Management Office does not mean that the RMB 3 million in land transfer fees had been or could be received. Subsequently, Qiankun Company did not cure the defect of this check. In fact, the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources did not receive this sum either. Since Qiankun Company was at fault for the invalidity of this check, it cannot be concluded that Qiankun Company's submission of this check constituted payment of the RMB 3 million land transfer fee. The Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources' defense regarding the invalidity of the check has factual and legal basis, and this Court should support it. The finding of the court of first instance that Qiankun Company had paid RMB 7.88 million in land transfer fees to the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources is erroneous and should be corrected.

To enforce the Civil Mediation Orders (2004) Lao Zhi Zi No. 297 and No. 1162, the Laoshan District People's Court, on March 25, 2005, deducted RMB 907,528 and RMB 2,905,829 from the land transfer deposits of the judgment debtor, Qiankun Company, held at the Beizhai Subdistrict Office, and transferred them to the court's account. On March 29 of the same year, the Beizhai Subdistrict Office sent a letter to Qiankun Company stating that the Laoshan District People's Court had forcibly deducted RMB 3,813,357 from the fiscal funds of the Beizhai Subdistrict Office, and that the Beizhai Subdistrict Office had already paid RMB 4,866,230 from the RMB 4.88 million in land transfer fees paid by Qiankun Company. Therefore, the finding of the court of first instance that the land transfer fee paid by Qiankun Company was RMB 4.88 million is correct. The land transfer fee payable by Qiankun Company should be calculated based on the land area of the valid part of the contract. The land transfer fee payable by Qiankun Company is RMB 5,782,089.6 (84 mu × 667 square meters × 103.2 yuan = 5,782,089.6 yuan). The paid amount of RMB 4.88 million is lower than the payable amount. Therefore, it should be found that Qiankun Company did not pay the full land transfer fee for the valid part of the contract.

(3) Whether the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources had the right to rescind the contract. The prerequisite for rescinding a contract is that the contract has taken effect. Article 31 of the State-owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract in question stipulates that if the transferee delays payment of the land transfer fee for more than six months, the transferor has the right to rescind the contract. The contract does not stipulate a period for exercising the right to rescind, nor does it require the transferor to make a demand for performance before rescinding the contract. Given that the contract is partially valid, Qiankun Company must perform its obligations within the scope of the valid part of the contract. The contract in question was signed on January 16, 2003. As of March 26, 2003, Qiankun Company had paid RMB 4.88 million in land transfer fees to the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources, which was less than the total transfer fee for the 84 mu of land. Therefore, the conditions for rescission of the contract had been met. The Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources exercised its right to rescind the contract pursuant to Article 93, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law and has notified Qiankun Company. The fact that it did not make a demand for performance to Qiankun Company does not constitute a breach of contract. This Court supports the claim of the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources that, because Qiankun Company failed to pay the full land transfer fee under the contract on time, it has the right to rescind the contract. This Court does not support Qiankun Company's claim that the conditions for rescission had not been met and that the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources had no right to unilaterally rescind the contract.

In summary, this Court holds: According to the agreement of the parties in the land transfer contract, the part of the contract that received government approval is valid, and the part that did not receive government approval is invalid. Both parties have an obligation to perform the valid part of the contract. Qiankun Company failed to perform its obligation to pay the land transfer fee for the valid part of the contract within the period stipulated in the contract. The conditions for rescission of the contract having been met, the rescission of the contract by the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources is valid. After the contract is rescinded, the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources is no longer obligated to transfer the use rights for the 84 mu of land to Qiankun Company. The appeal of the Laoshan Bureau of Land and Resources is well-founded, and this Court supports it. The court of first instance committed errors in fact-finding and improperly applied the law; accordingly, the judgment should be amended. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The claims of Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Court acceptance fees of RMB 160,778 for first instance and RMB 192,568.01 for second instance are all to be borne by Qingdao Qiankun Wood Industry Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
